claims.text_en: Khlong San is one of Bangkok's oldest khets, 6.051 km2 on the west bank's easternmost edge, with four khwaeng: Somdet Chao Phraya (1.317 km2, 11,444 people), Khlong San (0.727, 13,160), Bang Lamphu Lang (2.234, 22,471) and Khlong Ton Sai (1.773, 17,886) - 64,961 registered residents in Dec 2023 (Thai Wikipedia), 73,263 in 2017 (English Wikipedia). Boundaries: the Chao Phraya river on the north/east/south (across Phra Nakhon, Samphanthawong, Bang Rak, Sathon, Bang Kho Laem); the only land neighbour is Thon Buri, separated by Khlong Bang Sai Kai, Somdet Chao Phraya (Taksin) Road and Prajadhipok Road. History: originally Amphoe Bang Lamphu Lang, renamed Buppharam, then Khlong San (1916); named for the Khlong San/Prasan canal that once ran through longkong orchards, filled in roughly 70-80 years ago for Lat Ya, Prajadhipok and Khlong San roads; the Maeklong Railway's original terminus was here until the line was cut back to Wongwian Yai in 1961.

claims.text_en: Transit serving the khet (both wikis' lists): BTS Silom Line's Krung Thon Buri and Wongwian Yai stations, and the BTS Gold Line's three stops (Krung Thon Buri, Charoen Nakhon, Khlong San). Per the sibling st.khlong-san bundle, Gold Line G3 'Khlong San' (opened 16 Dec 2020, in front of Taksin Hospital) is the line's terminus and its OSM node sits inside the app district polygon; G2 Charoen Nakhon - the ICONSIAM stop - falls OUTSIDE the app district polygon, as does BTS Krung Thon Buri. Tha Din Daeng, Khlong San, Si Phraya (two gates), ICONSIAM 2/4 and other named ferry terminals are mapped along the khet's river frontage; both wikis list Tha Din Daeng and the Chao Phraya express-boat stops.

claims.text_en: ICONSIAM is the district's economic anchor: opened 9 November 2018 on a 30-rai riverside plot with roughly 50 billion THB invested, revenues reported at ~2,000M THB (2020-21), 3,747M (2022) and 5,385M (2024), with 51 new brands committing ~1,500M THB around the 2025 anniversary and an 'ICONSIAM 2' project teased. The mall sits in khwaeng Wat Kanlaya, Khet Khlong San (batch-3 found it inside st.charoen-nakhon's catchment within this district), but the app's khlong-san district polygon EXCLUDES the ICONSIAM/ICS/River Park points (PIP-verified) - a polygon-vs-administration conflict the coordinator must resolve.

claims.text_en: The 2021 Khlong San Plaza closure removed a 30-40-year-old wet-market/shopping staple: after the State Railway of Thailand raised the demanded rent from 1.6M to 15M THB, the operator declined renewal and began handing the ~5-rai site (adjacent to the cross-river ferry pier) back from 10 September 2021, with demolition to follow and SRT planning to re-auction the land; riverside land prices in the corridor had already risen to 400,000-500,000 THB/sq.wa, credited partly to the Gold Line. Nothing in body-read sources confirms a replacement anchor development on the plot as of 2026.

claims.text_en: Old communities vs riverside towers is the khet's defining texture: canal-orchard land filled for roads 70-80 years ago; heritage riverfront restorations (Lhong 1919 with its Mazu shrine, Wang Li House, Guan Yu shrine at the Princess Mother Memorial Park) sit among luxury towers (Magnolias at ICONSIAM noted by English Wikipedia as among Bangkok's tallest buildings); and in 2016 riverside households along the 7-km Chao Phraya promenade corridor were told to leave for at least 30,000 THB compensation, most without land titles. ICONSIAM's developer consulted 13 surrounding communities during 2012-2014. The 'mixture between local community and up-and-coming riverside district' reading in property copy matches the map: old sois inland of Somdet Chao Phraya and Charoen Nakhon, towers on the water.

question_answers.notes: Khet Khlong San, 6.051 km2, four khwaeng (Somdet Chao Phraya, Khlong San, Bang Lamphu Lang, Khlong Ton Sai with Dec-2023 populations 11,444/13,160/22,471/17,886), bounded by the river on three sides and by Khlong Bang Sai Kai/Taksin Rd/Prajadhipok Rd against Thon Buri. In-polygon anchors: Gold Line G3, Taksin Hospital, district office, Princess Mother Memorial Park, Wat Anongkharam, Wat Phichai Yat, PLATF@RM, Talat Tha Din Daeng. Excluded by the app polygon despite being administratively in-khet: ICONSIAM/ICS/River Park (khwaeng Wat Kanlaya), G2 Charoen Nakhon, Suan San park, Krung Thon bridge approaches, Sathorn Unique.

A west-bank residential khet stitched to a mega-mall riverfront: inland sois (Somdet Chao Phraya, Bang Lamphu Lang, Khlong Ton Sai) run temples, wet markets and old houses; the Charoen Nakhon/Wat Kanlaya strip carries ICONSIAM's decks, Gold Line stops and piers. Subarea claims marked partial - the mall is administratively in-khet but outside the app polygon.

Transport 9 = Gold Line-to-BTS hop + 11+ mapped piers + express boats + Krung Thon Buri/Wongwian Yai BTS (per wikis' serving lists). Vibe 9 = riverfront gravity (ICONSIAM's 5.4bn THB revenue) over a quiet residential grid. Food 9 = 970 POIs split between mall dining and soi kitchens. Rent 6 = luxury-skewed riverside pricing with a mid-market core (portal 1-bed ~USD 592).

Green 7 on 5.3 ha (0.9%) is the weakest value: the khet's own named public green is small, the riverside park is private-mall ground, and the big green names sit at polygon edges or across boundaries. The 2021 Khlong San Plaza closure removed a 40-year everyday-market anchor with no confirmed replacement. The app polygon itself contradicts several in-khet landmark memberships.

Commute pulses via G3 and the BTS at morning/evening; mall evenings and weekend riverfront crowds at ICONSIAM (revenue-driven footfall); residential sois quiet otherwise, thinning further as registered population falls (73,263 in 2017 -> 64,961 in 2023); everything except the riverfront winds down early.

Flat river-bend grid; the Gold Line terminus sits at Taksin Hospital's door on Somdet Chao Phraya frontage, markets and piers line the river roads, and inland sois are block-scale walking. No walking durations were derived from catchment radius in this bundle; the app polygon's coarseness means walking statements describe the khet, not the polygon.

Daily needs: Talat Tha Din Daeng and inland sois + mall-grade retail at ICONSIAM/ICS; health: Taksin Hospital (BMA) and Somdet Chao Phraya Institute of Psychiatry (PIP-IN); heritage leisure: Princess Mother Memorial Park, Lhong 1919, Wat Anongkharam; river crossing by ferry or two bridges (Taksin, Phra Pok Klao).

App 20,000/45,000 sits between the riverside-skewed portal means (HipFlat 1-bed USD 592 ~ 20-21k THB at 34-35 THB/USD; 2-bed USD 1,245 ~ 42-44k) and the inland mid-market stock; prices falling (-9.7% vs Jan 2026). Consistent reading: riverfront premium + soft inland band averages out to the blend; rent 6 is fair only if the inland half is what a renter actually gets.

Green: 5.3 ha app vs small mapped public green (Princess Mother Memorial Park complex the main in-polygon piece; Suan San park and Somdet Ya park at edges; ICONSIAM River Park private). Green 7 depends on borrowed riverfront/canal-edge amenities - honest only with that caveat. Quiet: real inland of the riverfront; the mall's weekend footfall does not reach the sois.

Strong fit: renters who want a residential west-bank address with riverfront weekends, a one-hop BTS commute, and mid-to-upper rents. Weak fit: park users (0.9% park share), bargain hunters (riverside premium), or anyone expecting the app polygon's landmarks to match administrative Khlong San (ICONSIAM excluded by polygon).

ICONSIAM revenue growth to 5,385M THB (2024) with 51 new brands (~1,500M THB) and a teased 'ICONSIAM 2' (Sept 2025); portal rents per sqm down ~9.7% during 2026; the former Khlong San Plaza land still without a confirmed anchor as of 2026 in body-read sources.

Unresolved: ICONSIAM's polygon membership (administratively in, polygon out - coordinator call); the app's 5.3-ha park counting rule; which piers the app counts (OSM shows 11+ named terminals); whether any development has risen on the plaza plot; PropertyScout corroboration failed (404) so HipFlat is the sole rent source. Safety 7 untested by any located statistic.

preview.text_en: Old west-bank canalside sois on one side, ICONSIAM's billion-dollar riverfront on the other - Khlong San is the rare khet where a mega-mall is your neighbourhood amenity and your nearest public park is a memorial garden.

guide_lead.text_en: Khlong San wraps four khwaeng of west-bank sois, temples and piers around the Charoen Nakhon riverfront, where ICONSIAM (opened 2018, revenues up to 5.4bn THB in 2024) sets the register for everything from rents to dining. Transit is unusually deep for the west bank - the Gold Line's Khlong San terminus at Taksin Hospital, BTS Silom stops, express boats and 11+ mapped piers - while public green is thin (5.3 ha, 0.9%). The 2021 loss of the 40-year Khlong San Plaza market to an SRT rent dispute marked the turn from market-khet to tower-khet; registered population has fallen to 64,961.

strengths.text_en: Transit depth without a rail-hub address: a Gold Line terminus at Taksin Hospital, BTS Silom stops at both ends of the khet, two bridges and a dense pier layer for river commuting.
The riverfront-amenity trade: mall-grade dining, retail and river decks at ICONSIAM/ICS alongside heritage anchors (Lhong 1919, Princess Mother Memorial Park) that cost nothing to visit.

tradeoffs.text_en: Green 7 is buffer-dependent: the khet holds just 5.3 ha of park (0.9% share), the riverside 'park' is private mall ground, and the named public parks sit at polygon edges.
The everyday-market layer lost its 40-year anchor when Khlong San Plaza closed in 2021 over an SRT rent jump (1.6M -> 15M THB), and no replacement development is confirmed.

conditional_fit.text_en: Choose it if you want river-adjacent living with real transit (Gold Line + BTS + boats) at rents starting around 15k for studios and ~42-44k for 2-beds near the water - and can live with pocket-scale parks.
Skip it if you need actual park acreage or a cheap everyday-market street: at 0.9% park share and with the plaza market gone, the green and market stories are the khet's weakest.
